item.title: Jimmy Carr breaks silence on controversial ‘career-ender’ Holocaust joke that nearly got him cancelled
item.description: Jimmy Carr addressed the controversy surrounding his Holocaust joke from his Netflix special, "His Dark Material," in a recent interview. He explained the joke was intended to highlight lesser-known victims and was taken out of context by viral clips. Carr maintained his intent was not literal and that the audience understood this, despite criticism from politicians and advocacy groups.

Minority groups protest over failure to stop persecution
item.description: Minority groups in Bangladesh have accused the government of failing to protect them from violence and persecution, citing the brutal killing of a garment worker for alleged blasphemy. Leaders called for the chief advisor's removal, alleging state patronage of divisive forces and militant groups. Media organizations also protested recent attacks, demanding justice for perpetrators.

item.title: Zia's son, in exile for 17 years, to return to Bangladesh on December 25
item.description: Tarique Rahman, son of former Bangladesh PM Khaleda Zia, is set to return from self-exile in the UK on December 25. His return fuels speculation he may lead the BNP in upcoming parliamentary polls due to his mother's health. Rahman will also complete voter registration formalities upon his arrival.

MAGA rift: Heritage Foundation staff walk out after president defends Tucker Carlson interview with Nick Fuentes
item.description: More than a dozen employees have resigned from the Heritage Foundation following president Kevin Roberts' defense of Tucker Carlson's interview with Nick Fuentes. This exodus, including senior staff and board members, highlights deep divisions within the conservative movement over extremism and leadership. Many defectors have joined Mike Pence's Advancing American Freedom, signaling a broader MAGA identity crisis.

item.title: Real-life Stranger Things: Girl who went to explore Hawkins Lab site dies after falling from building
item.description: A 19-year-old girl tragically died after falling from the abandoned Briarcliff Building, famously used as Hawkins National Laboratory in Stranger Things. Leah Palmirotto entered the fenced-off, deteriorating site with friends despite clear warnings. Authorities are investigating the exact cause of the fall, emphasizing the severe risks of exploring such dangerous locations.

item.title: French court rejects nationwide Kick ban following Jean Pormanove’s death
item.description: A French court has refused to block the livestreaming platform Kick nationwide following the death of streamer Jean Pormanove. While authorities sought a six-month ban due to concerns over harmful content, the court deemed it too extreme. Instead, the focus will be on targeting specific accounts or content if necessary, as Kick remains under criminal investigation.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Trump’s Greenland obsession gets official: President taps MAGA ally as Greenland envoy; Denmark warns on sovereignty
item.description: President Trump nominated a MAGA ally as the first special envoy to Greenland, a newly created role stemming from his long-standing interest in the island. This move sparked alarm in Denmark, which insists on respecting Greenland's territorial integrity. The appointment, described as a volunteer position, aims to advance U.S. interests and security in the strategically important Arctic region.

item.title: Marjorie Taylor Greene says Venezuela’s Maduro critical of Israel, opposition Maria Corina Machado backs strong ties with Jerusalem
item.description: US Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene highlighted a stark contrast between Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his opponent Maria Corina Machado regarding their stances on Israel. Greene stated Maduro has criticized Israel's actions in Gaza, while Machado is a strong supporter. Greene also noted Machado's more liberal views on abortion and LGBTQ+ issues, suggesting American voters are wary of foreign intervention.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Disturbing new Epstein photos spark outrage: What US DOJ has released, what’s still hidden
item.description: Thousands of documents and disturbing images from the Jeffrey Epstein investigation have been released by the DOJ, sparking outrage and renewed scrutiny. While intended for transparency, the heavily redacted files and selective removals have drawn criticism, fueling debate over accountability and the extent of government disclosure. The fallout continues to dominate public discourse.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Diane Crawford? School bus driver dismissed after posting ‘English-only’ sign in Pennsylvania; Indian-origin Dhillon opens probe
item.description: A school bus driver was fired after posting a sign in her bus window stating, "Out of respect to English-only students, there will be no speaking Spanish on this bus." The driver, Diane Crawford, claimed her intention was to create a safe environment, not to be racially insensitive. The Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division will reportedly investigate her termination.

item.title: Woman blends every meal and eats by snorting food through her nose
item.description: A new season of My Strange Addiction returns in January, led by Kathryn, a woman from Virginia who blends and snorts every meal through her nose after a college dare. Her episode follows her as she prepares to tell her new boyfriend about the habit, while early footage has already sparked shock, disbelief and alarm among viewers online.

item.title: Candace Owens shares shocking fresh witness claim about Erika Kirk meeting security before Charlie Kirk death
item.description: Candace Owens shared claims from a former special forces witness who says he saw Erika Kirk and security chief Brian Harpole at Fort Huachuca before Charlie Kirk’s reported death. The claims were made on Owens’ podcast and remain unverified. No police or federal agency has confirmed the account so far.
